about.description:
A pure Python module to calculate light scattering for
non-absorbing, partially-absorbing, or perfectly-conducting spheres. Mie
theory is used, following the procedure described by Wiscombe
<http://opensky.ucar.edu/islandora/object/technotes:232>. This code has
been validated against his results.

This code provides functions for calculating the extinction efficiency,
scattering efficiency, backscattering, and scattering asymmetry. Moreover,
a set of angles can be given to calculate the scattering for a sphere at
each of those angles.
about.summary: Mie scattering of a plane wave by a homogeneous sphere

commands: python -c "import os; os.environ['MIEPYTHON_USE_JIT'] = '1'; import miepython; assert miepython.USE_JIT; print(miepython.efficiencies_mx(1.5 - 0.1j, 1.0))"

name: miepython
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "miepython" %}
{% set version = "3.3.0" %}
{% set python_min = "3.10" %}

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/{{ name[0] }}/{{ name }}/miepython-{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 391ebf3f033ca941ffb47db0b75d508761452fa3d8fb145e0cdca80c191003e3

build:
  noarch: python
  script: {{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  number: 1

requirements:
  # pure python, so the build needs nothing but the build backend; numpy and
  # scipy are imported at run time only
  host:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - setuptools >=77
    - wheel
  run:
    - python >={{ python_min }}
    - matplotlib-base
    - numba
    - numpy
    - scipy

test:
  imports:
    - miepython
    - miepython.rayleigh
    - miepython.monte_carlo
  requires:
    - python {{ python_min }}
    - pip
    - pytest
  source_files:
    # the whole directory: conftest.py picks the backend and reference.py holds
    # the independent implementations the tests compare against
    - tests/
  commands:
    - pip check
    # two files need a source checkout rather than an installed package:
    # test_all_examples.py globs miepython/examples, and test_all_notebooks.py
    # reads docs/*.ipynb through nbformat.  Neither ships in the sdist.
    - pytest tests -p no:cacheprovider --ignore=tests/test_all_examples.py --ignore=tests/test_all_notebooks.py
    # the suite above runs the pure-python kernels; MIEPYTHON_USE_JIT has to be
    # set before miepython is imported, so exercise the numba path from python
    - python -c "import os; os.environ['MIEPYTHON_USE_JIT'] = '1'; import miepython; assert miepython.USE_JIT; print(miepython.efficiencies_mx(1.5 - 0.1j, 1.0))"

about:
  home: https://github.com/scottprahl/miepython
  summary: Mie scattering of a plane wave by a homogeneous sphere
  description: |
    A pure Python module to calculate light scattering for
    non-absorbing, partially-absorbing, or perfectly-conducting spheres. Mie
    theory is used, following the procedure described by Wiscombe
    <http://opensky.ucar.edu/islandora/object/technotes:232>. This code has
    been validated against his results.

    This code provides functions for calculating the extinction efficiency,
    scattering efficiency, backscattering, and scattering asymmetry. Moreover,
    a set of angles can be given to calculate the scattering for a sphere at
    each of those angles.
  license: MIT
  license_family: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.txt
  doc_url: https://miepython.readthedocs.io/
  dev_url: https://github.com/scottprahl/miepython

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - scottprahl
